name: uv-cpp
baseline: Boost.Asio 1.67 (TCP ping-pong echo); nginx 1.14.2 (HTTP, Apache bench, chart images only)
workload: Loopback TCP ping-pong echo throughput in kbyte per second at 1K/2K/4K/8K bytes per packet, and with 10/100/1000/5000 concurrent connections at 4K bytes, uv-cpp (libuv 1.30.0 wrapper) against a Boost.Asio 1.67 echo server; a second comparison runs Apache bench against uv-cpp's HTTP server and nginx 1.14.2 with 1000 concurrency and 100000 requests.
claimed_speedup: README table, kbyte (throughput units as printed; uv-cpp vs boost.asio): packet size 1K 16138 vs 16119 (+0.1%, derived from page data), 2K 32071 vs 31566 (+1.6%, derived), 4K 59264 vs 58322 (+1.6%, derived), 8K 123813 vs 126210 (-1.9%, derived: asio faster). Concurrency at 4K bytes: 10 conns 654282 vs 633818 (+3.2%, derived), 100 conns 591869 vs 585716 (+1.1%, derived), 1000 conns 401500 vs 371386 (+8.1%, derived), 5000 conns 412855 vs 382402 (+8.0%, derived). nginx comparison is two chart images (uv_http_1000.png, nginx_http_1000.png) with no numbers in the text.
compiler_and_flags: gcc 8.3.0, '-O2', libuv 1.30.0, Boost.Asio 1.67 (README environment line: Intel Core i5 8265U + debian8 + gcc8.3.0 + libuv1.30.0 + '-O2')
hardware: Intel Core i5 8265U (second table also lists 4G memory); loopback on one machine
tradeoffs: Thin C++11 callback wrapper over libuv (bundled libuv 1.30.0), so it inherits libuv's single-loop model and adds TCP, UDP, DNS, HTTP server with radix-tree routing, timers, timer wheel, packet framing. Not header-only; Linux and Windows only.
caveats: First-party, tier C. The ping-pong code is public (examples/pingpang for uv-cpp, examples/boost_asio_echo_server and boost_asio_echo_client for Asio) but not parameterized to the README tables: the uv-cpp example sends one 1024-byte message, uses CycleBuffer packet framing (Packet header pack and unpack per message) and prints a message count per second, while the Asio server echoes raw bytes and prints kbyte/s, so the two programs do different work and the README numbers came from modified runs that are not in the repo. Gaps are small (0.1% to 8%) with no repeat counts or variance stated, uv-cpp is slower at 8K packets (-1.9% derived), and numbers come from one 2019-era laptop-class CPU on loopback with Boost.Asio 1.67 (old). Build flags for the Asio binary are not stated separately from the shared environment line. The nginx 1.14.2 comparison exists only as images that were not readable, so no nginx number is recorded. The comparison is libuv-based wrapper versus Asio, not versus a C++ standard-library facility.
